title: Bounded arithmetic: truth tests and proof construction

based_on.title: An Introduction to Gödel's Theorems, second edition, corrected Logic Matters reprint

summary: Build numerical and bounded-formula proof certificates with explicit internal loop invariants.
abstract: A bounded arithmetic statement can be tested by a finite calculation. Turning that calculation into a proof requires more information: each step must produce a proof record that the actual PA checker accepts. We build certificates for addition, multiplication and comparisons, then use them for formulas with bounded quantifiers. A true universal statement needs a loop assembling all its instances, while a false one needs a checked counterexample. Explicit induction invariants make these procedures work at arbitrary internal bounds. The result is a pair of proof-building procedures for every fixed bounded formula, one for truth and one for falsity, whose correctness PA itself proves.
